title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: the last Kaurava king walks into a lake, and some hunters overhear
tomorrow: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shalya fell to Yudhishthira's dart, and Sahadeva kept his vow against Shakuni. Your line was the vow from that hall is kept.

One man walks away from the battlefield on foot, carrying a mace. His horse is dead. His army is gone. His brothers, his friends, his commanders have fallen. He is the king the whole war was fought for, and he is alone. On the way he meets Sanjaya, his father's companion, and gives him a message for the blind old king at home: tell my father I've gone into the lake. Then Duryodhana walks down to the water's edge, and keeps walking.
screen: `ALONE, ON FOOT.` → `TELL MY FATHER.` → `INTO THE LAKE.`

segments.voice: In Ganguli's English, Duryodhana enters the lake and, by a power of illusion he knows, binds the waters around him, so that he can rest beneath them, hidden. It's an eerie picture: the lake smooth and still, and the last Kaurava king lying under it. Three survivors of his army find the lake: Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma. They call down to him from the bank. Come out, fight with us. From under the water he answers: not tonight. I'm wounded and tired. Tomorrow. Then the epic brings in some passersby: hunters, men who bring meat to Bhima's kitchen. They hear the whole conversation, a king speaking from under a lake, and they think: the Pandavas are searching everywhere for Duryodhana, and Bhima will reward us. So they go and tell him. The war's last hiding place is given away by a few hunters with a delivery to make. The Pandavas come to the lake with Krishna, and their army fills the shore with noise. Yudhishthira stands at the edge of the still water and speaks to his cousin underneath it. Why are you hiding? Come out and fight. Duryodhana answers from below: I'm not afraid. I'm only resting.
screen: `HE BINDS THE WATERS` · `THREE SURVIVORS CALL DOWN` · `THE HUNTERS OVERHEAR` · then, large: `WHY ARE YOU HIDING?`

segments.voice: Let your body grow still, the way a lake does when the wind drops. Notice whether some part of you has been hiding lately, under busyness, wanting not to be found, and let it rest there without dragging it out. If you pray, you can bring it quietly into your prayer.
Shalya. The book of the war's last day: the commander fallen, and Duryodhana lying hidden under a lake until hunters give him away.
Your line: not afraid, only resting. Tomorrow, an offer from under the water. Day eight hundred forty-five, done.

notes: Editor pass: replaced the narrator's verdict 'small and perfect' with a plain transition.
All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli Duryodhana's message to Sanjaya and his binding (Ganguli: 'stupefying') of the waters by illusion.
Confirm that the three survivors are Kripa, Ashvatthama and Kritavarma, and that Duryodhana asks to rest until the next day.
Confirm that the hunters supplied meat to Bhima and told him in hope of reward.
The lake is named Dvaipayana in the text; the script leaves the name out.
Duryodhana's reply ('not afraid, only resting') is paraphrased; tomorrow's script (day 846) continues the conversation.
